text:
The DC bias fault points to M5, the tail current source. Its operating point is inconsistent with the mirror it should follow: M6 is the diode-connected reference (W/L = 0.49/2.34) and M5 has W/L = 2.02/2.34, so M5 should carry about 4.1× the reference current (~41 µA). Instead, M5 carries 26.7 µA and sits in triode (Vds = 0.226 V < Vdsat = 0.546 V). The tail node is pulled low, so M5 cannot act as a current source, which collapses the input pair's bias and the gain and swing. The other mirrors check out: M8 (2.2× M6) carries 22.6 µA, close to its expected 22 µA.

The f0 failure (about 20 MHz against a 25–31 Hz target) is set by the passive RC network, which has time constants around 10⁻⁸ s. The sensitivity list doesn't include the passives, so I can't confirm from it whether a passive was also changed. The M5 fault is the one that explains the device-level symptoms. M2 and M4 rank next because they appear in the f0 sensitivity list and sit in the signal path of the same stage.

```json
{"ranking": ["M5", "M2", "M4"], "fault": "M5 (tail current source) is mis-sized relative to the M6 reference mirror (W/L ratio 2.02/2.34 vs. the expected ~4.1x of the 0.49/2.34 reference). Its tail current is 26.7 uA rather than ~41 uA, and it operates in triode (Vds 0.226 V < Vdsat 0.546 V). The tail node is pulled low, which breaks the input-pair bias, gain and swing. Restore M5 to saturation with the intended mirror ratio. The f0 error (~2e7 Hz vs 25-31 Hz) is set by the passive RC values and was not explained by any device fault, so it should be checked separately."}
```
